_README: Every question the welcome interview asks, in one machine-readable file.
WHY THIS EXISTS: onboarding is a conversation, but a conversation isn't
repeatable. Fill this in once and you can rebuild the whole system from
scratch — stamp, hand the lead this file, done — then tear it down and do
it again identically. That makes onboarding testable instead of a
one-shot interview you hope went right.
HOW TO USE IT (three ways, all valid):
1. Ignore it. DM the lead and answer conversationally. This file is
never required.
2. Fill it in first, then tell the lead: 'my answers are in
/workspace/agent/onboarding-answers.json'. It reads, echoes back a
summary, asks only about what's still null, and persists.
3. Fill in part of it. The lead uses what's here and asks only about
what's missing or null.
This copy is filled in with ChurchCRM's real, verified answers — from
actual installs, not invented — because a worked example beats an empty
template. Replace every value for your own project before using it.
NEVER PUT A SECRET IN THIS FILE. No API keys, tokens, passwords, or
webhook URLs — ever. Secrets live only in the OneCLI vault; this file is
config (repo names, channel ids, preferences). It is safe to commit to a
private repo, and scripts/check-onboarding.sh fails if anything in it
looks like a credential.
'persists_to' tells you where each answer ends up. config.env keys are
read by bash gate scripts; project_config keys are prose the agent reads,
four of which setup-check.sh greps literally. Getting these two
namespaces backwards is the #1 cause of 'I answered that but nothing
happened'.
AUTO-DETECTED FIELDS (marked below): the welcome interview checks these
against the repo itself before asking — has_wiki, README-linked social
URLs, .github/dependabot.yml, SECURITY.md, a Discord invite badge. Filled
in here with what was actually found and confirmed on a real install, not
guessed — a wrong guess (e.g. a constructed social URL slug) fails
silently where a real extracted link doesn't.

agents_to_stamp._ask: Which agents do you want? 'manager' (the lead, opensource/community-manager) is required — it's the only agent with a public voice, and it stamps the others itself once it knows which jobs you want. 'secretary' is the recommended second: it owns unanswered-watch, the task that keeps the community from hearing silence when the lead is rate-limited. 'coding' and 'marketing' are optional.
agents_to_stamp._note: Not a one-way door — add or pause any of these later without redoing this file. This real install stamped all four.

timezone._ask: Your IANA timezone, e.g. America/New_York or Europe/Berlin.
timezone._format: IANA zone name — not an offset like UTC-5, which cannot handle daylight saving.
timezone._note: This is NOT a stamp-time decision anymore — `ncl groups config update --timezone <id>` changes it live, no restart, no recreate (see docs/INSTALL.md). OWNER_TZ specifically drives owner-tldr's 'is it the owner's morning yet' check; it's separate from each group's own container timezone.

daily_digest_local_hour._ask: What local hour should the daily owner-tldr digest land at? Real answer here: 'up by 7 AM'.

primary_github_repo._ask: The project's main GitHub repo — everything else is inferred from this. Format owner/repo.

repo_map._ask: Per function: which repo, and a subpath if it isn't the repo root. Functions often SHARE one repo — don't assume separate repos. This project doesn't: all five are genuinely separate.
_derives: config.env:COMMUNITY_REPOS — repos to triage (issues/PRs/advisories/metrics), set on manager, secretary, and coding.
config.env:MIRROR_REPOS — the full repo map (including wiki) for repo-mirror-sync to keep checked out. secretary only.
config.env:CONTENT_REPO — where content drafts get committed and PR'd. Needed by marketing (writes) and secretary (reads, for draft-cleanup).
config.env:PRODUCT_REPO — the main repo. coding's docs-currency-watch watches its merged PRs.
config.env:DOCS_REPO / DOCS_PATH — where docs-currency-watch opens its PR; DOCS_PATH only if docs are a subdirectory rather than their own repo.

docs._note: docs is its own repo here, not a subpath — subpath's value persists to config.env:DOCS_PATH only when docs live inside the product repo instead.

wiki._note: Auto-detected via has_wiki:true on the GET /repos/ChurchCRM/CRM call — never probe {repo}.wiki as its own API resource, that gives a false negative even when the wiki exists (confirmed bug, see UPSTREAM-ISSUES.md).

target_audience_and_tone.value: Church administrative and IT staff running the software day to day — not developers, not general consumers. Warm, practical, plain-language register; no engineering jargon, no growth-hacker marketing voice.
target_audience_and_tone._ask: Who's the primary reader of your content, and what tone follows from it? Don't infer this from the README — ask plainly.

docs_style.value: current behavior only, no version-history language
docs_style._ask: Should docs describe current behavior only, or is version-history language ('added in 4.5') fine? Real answer here: current-only, because users are pushed to stay upgraded.

channels._note: Discord. Auto-approve unknown senders on every community channel (unknown_sender_policy=public) — the owner DM stays locked to known senders regardless.

discord_invite_url._ask: Auto-detected from the README/site — verify it's live against Discord's API before trusting it. This project's SECURITY.md ALSO references a second, dead invite code (discord.gg/XGppbeTw) — the auto-detection caught that discrepancy and flagged it rather than silently picking one.

team_lead_mention_only._note: announcements is the release-announcement-watch target — confirm this explicitly if more than one channel is in this tier.

holding_ack._ask: Which channel should the secretary's holding acknowledgment post to when the lead is rate-limited, and how long a message can sit unanswered first? Real answer here: support-chat (busiest support channel), 0 minutes — 'do it real time', no delay, not the 20-minute skill default.

disclosure_path._ask: Auto-detected from SECURITY.md before asking — confirm what it says rather than asking from scratch.

escalation_backstop.value: none — sole maintainer, recorded as an open risk
escalation_backstop._ask: Who is the second human — a moderator or co-maintainer with a name and contact — that abuse reports and urgent escalations should reach when you aren't reachable? Asked always; 'no one yet' is a complete answer, recorded as an open risk, not silently accepted.

watch_scope._ask: Optional narrower subset of COMMUNITY_REPOS for security-advisory-sweep — docs/content repos rarely have dependencies worth a sweep.

dependabot.value: already configured — Dependabot opens its own version-update PRs (npm, composer, github-actions); the Reviewer reviews the diff, doesn't draft the bump
dependabot._ask: Auto-detected from .github/dependabot.yml before asking — if a version-updates config already exists, that answers the question.
dependabot._note: DEPENDABOT_REVIEW_MAX itself is an optional tuning cap, not this decision — leave at task default unless you have a reason to change it.

social._note: Auto-detected from the README as literal URLs, not constructed from a display name — a display name and a URL slug are often different strings (this project's own accounts are @getChurchCRM / linkedin.com/company/getchurchcrm, not a guess from 'ChurchCRM').

posting_mechanism.value: manual — marketing drafts content as PRs to ChurchCRM/marketing; owner reviews, approves, and posts by hand
posting_mechanism._ask: Per platform: which exist, which the project actually posts to, and the mechanism — intent-URL (free, default), manual copy-paste, or paid API (owner's explicit opt-in only; X has no free tier since Feb 2026).

release_watch_repo._ask: Only if the release-watch repo (marketing's content-draft-cycle) differs from CONTENT_REPO.

release_watch_repos_lead._ask: Optional narrower subset of COMMUNITY_REPOS to scope the LEAD's release-announcement-watch (plural key — distinct from marketing's singular RELEASE_WATCH_REPO above). Falls back to COMMUNITY_REPOS if unset.

brand_source_repo._ask: Only if the brand/strategy source repo differs from CONTENT_REPO.

github_actions_discord_notify._ask: Want a ready-made GitHub Actions workflow that posts bug/security-labeled issues straight to Discord, independent of the lead's own uptime? Needs two webhook secrets added to the repo. See examples/github-discord-notify.yml.

ga4_property_ids._ask: GA4 property id — 'not now' is a fine answer, the task silent-skips until configured. This project has two (www.churchcrm.io, Demo Installs) — one weekly-analytics-report task covers both in a single run; don't create a separate task per property.

good_first_issue_label._ask: Which label marks a good-first-issue on this repo?

models._note: Defaults offered per agent; confirm or name a different model. Real answer here: defaults across the board.

manager._note: no cheaper option offered — this is the one identity the community sees

secretary._note: cloud default; a local-model provider was evaluated and set aside, see SKILLS-ADOPTION.md

coding._note: or Sonnet for stronger judgment on drafts, at more cost

marketing._note: no cheaper option — weak drafts nobody wants published

github_bot_username._ask: The dedicated bot account's GitHub username — never the owner's own. Every GitHub token's identity gets checked against this mechanically (a real GET /user call), not just recorded.

onecli_dashboard_url._ask: Same machine as this conversation, or a reachable remote address (e.g. a Tailscale IP) for checking in from elsewhere? Left null here deliberately — network addresses are host-specific and shouldn't be copied between installs.

workspace_backup_repo._ask: A private repo the config/ledgers get pushed to (secretary does the pushing). 'skip' is a complete answer, but it's the only thing that survives a recreate.

_tuning_defaults_not_asked_conversationa._note: Internal gate-script tuning caps with sane built-in defaults. Only override if a real problem shows up — not part of the interview.
